title: Attenuated IAM Profiles and SIEM Export Contracts
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact set of IAM role profiles (attentuated roles) mapped to environment-specific constraints (hosted / dedicated / private), and the expected SIEM export contract (audit log schema + delivery semantics). The goal is to enable automated evidence collection and consistent ingestion into downstream analysis systems (Splunk/Elastic/Datadog) while enforcing least-privilege by default.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform security, infra, SRE, product security reviewers, and compliance engineers.
- Scope: RBAC role definitions for runtime and operational surfaces, audit log schema fields required for evidence, automated evidence generation patterns, and SIEM export topics/mappings per deployment mode. This doc does not include low-level cloud-provider JSON examples for every service (those live in the policy templates repo) but provides canonical snippets and mapping rules.

High-level principles:
1) Attenuation by default: prefer narrow, task-oriented roles (e.g., model-infer-runner) instead of broad surface roles (e.g., gpu-admin).
2) Environment scoping: every role must include an environment tag (env:hosted|dedicated|private) and a tenant scoping mechanism for multi-tenant hosted customers.
3) Evidence-first design: every control must emit a minimal audit record (see schema) and tie to a verifiable evidence artifact (signed request id, certificate thumbprint).
4) Export contract stability: SIEM export topics and field names are stable for 12 months unless explicitly versioned.

Attenuated role profiles (summary):
- infra-readonly: read-only across infra objects (metrics, topology); no write actions. Allowed in hosted & dedicated; restricted in private (only ops-approved service accounts).
- model-infer-runner: scoped to a single model-version and GPU pool; actions: SubmitInference, ReadKVCacheStats, StreamResponse. Allowed in all environments but with stronger network egress controls in private.
- deployment-operator: create/update rollout objects, can trigger canaries. Allowed in dedicated/private; in hosted this role maps to a service-managed operator service principal (customer cannot directly hold it).
- evidence-exporter: service account that can read audit-log streams and push to external SIEM endpoints (Splunk/ELK/Datadog). Only allowed in dedicated and private (hosted uses Redwood-managed export endpoints).
- tenant-admin (hosted): tenant-scoped admin with ability to manage keys and access for that tenant only; cannot modify cluster-level roles or export configs.
- emergency-priv: break-glass time-limited role with MFA and justification flow; automatically expires after 4 hours and emits explicit evidence record for compliance review.

Role-to-policy mapping notes (short):
- Prefer action lists over wildcard resources. Example policy snippet (text):
  {
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["inference:Submit","inference:StreamGet"],
    "Resource": ["arn:redwood:inference:gpu-pool:${pool_id}:model:${model_id}"]
  }
- Use "Condition" clauses for environment scoping: env=="dedicated" or tenantId=="${tenant}".
- Attach metadata tags to roles: created_by, approval_ticket, expiry_days.

Environment-specific constraints and examples:
- Hosted:
  - No direct public export credentials for customer-managed SIEM. Exports are routed through Redwood-managed exporters with per-tenant filters.
  - Tenant-admin cannot escalate to cluster-admin.
  - Audit samples: session_id, tenant_id, api_key_hash, route, model_version, latency_ms.
- Dedicated:
  - Customers may request export credentials; require evidence-exporter role with scoped network allowlist.
  - Dedicated pools may enable privileged debug mode under explicit approval; all debug operations require emergency-priv invocation.
- Private:
  - Private deployments can host their own SIEM exporters; recommended pattern is push to local syslog or kafka topic.
  - Certain telemetry fields may be redacted by default (customer PII).

Audit log schema (minimal required fields):
- event_id: UUIDv4 (string)
- timestamp_utc: ISO-8601 (string)
- principal: principal_type:principal_id (string) e.g. service:infra-agent or user:alice@redwood.ai
- principal_auth_method: api_key | oauth | mfa | svc_cert (string)
- action: canonical_action_name (string) e.g., inference.submit, rollout.create
- resource: resource_arn or resource_path (string)
- outcome: success | failure | denied (string)
- reason: short textual description (string) - required for denied/failure
- env: hosted | dedicated | private (string)
- tenant_id: if applicable, otherwise "-" (string)
- request_id: persisted request id for traceability (string)
- evidence_refs: list of artifact ids (list of strings) e.g., ["evidence:sign-req-...","logs:s3://..." ]
- correlation_tags: list of short strings for grouping (list of strings)
- token_cost_estimate: estimated_token_units (string) optional but recommended for billing-attached events

Notes about schema usage and redaction:
- PII must not be included in free-text fields; if necessary, hash with purpose and salt.
- evidence_refs should be resolvable by the compliance UI; store pointers not full artifacts in the stream.

SIEM export topics and mapping (contract):
- Export topic names (stable):
  - redwood.activity.events.v1 (primary audit events stream)
  - redwood.evidence.artifacts.v1 (attachments and signed artifacts metadata)
  - redwood.system.health.v1 (uptime, infra incidents)
- Mapping guidance to consumer fields (example for Elastic/Splunk):
  - redwood.activity.events.v1 -> index: redwood-events-%{env}  fields: event_id,timestamp_utc,principal,action,resource,outcome,tenant_id,env,correlation_tags
  - redwood.evidence.artifacts.v1 -> index: redwood-evidence  fields: artifact_id,attached_to_event_id,storage_uri,hash,created_by,ttl_days
- Delivery semantics:
  - Exactly-once-ish: exporters should use idempotent writes keyed by event_id. A best-effort retry with dedupe keys is required.
  - Batching: default payload batch <= 500 events or 2MB per POST for hosted exporters to avoid timeouts.

Evidence automation runbook (high-level):
1) Event emitted -> local logger attaches request_id and short binary blob reference -> upload artifact to evidence-store (S3/kafka) -> store artifact metadata in evidence.artifacts topic.
2) Evidence exporter picks artifacts older than 30s, bundles by tenant, and pushes into customer SIEM (or Redwood-managed endpoint).
3) Compliance job reconciles exported events vs expected export snapshot every 24h; discrepancies open a ticket (jira:SEC-EXPORT-DIFF).

Retention and TTLs:
- Audit events: default 13 months for hosted and dedicated; configurable for private.
- Evidence artifacts (attachments): default 90 days, with policy to archive to cold storage for 2 years on request.
- Emergency-priv justification logs: stored for 3 years.

Sample policy template (text snippet, developer-friendly):
- Emergency-priv activation policy:
  POST /v1/ops/elevate -> requires mfa: "mfa:required", justification text <= 1024 chars.
  Response: elevation_token (short-lived, 4h) attached to principal in audit event.

Change and rollout playbook (summary):
- Phase 1: Define canonical roles and publish JSON snippets to infra/policies repo (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: Implement SIEM exporters for redwood.activity.events.v1 and redwood.evidence.artifacts.v1 (3 weeks).
- Phase 3: Pilot with one dedicated customer; collect feedback and adjust retention/export filters (4 weeks).
- Phase 4: Global rollout for hosted with communication to customers and migration window (8 weeks).

Open questions / decisions required:
- Confirm maximum permitted retention for hosted customer audit events (legal to advise).
- Decide whether evidence_refs should embed an HMAC for offline verification.
- Approve export topic naming convention versioning policy beyond v1.

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers:
- Do all roles include env scoping and tenant scoping where applicable? (Y/N)
- Are all denied/failure outcomes emitting a non-empty reason field? (Y/N)
- Are emergency-priv activations time-limited and audited with justification? (Y/N)
- Is the export contract documented with field-level types and example indexed mapping? (Y/N)

If this doc looks good, next step: convert the role summaries into concrete JSON policy files in infra/policies and open PRs for the exporter code changes (github:infra/siem-exporter).

Notes to self: keep field names stable and add schema version header to every export message (e.g., schema_version: "1.0.0").
